text:
nora-finance: Morning  invoice from Analytica Labs Pvt Ltd (IN) landed. Vendor is asking Redwood to gross-up because they expect US withholding if paid by Redwood, Inc. Need tax guidance and next steps.

nora-finance: Invoice summary:
```
INV-AL-0326
Vendor: Analytica Labs Pvt Ltd, GSTIN 27ALYTI1234A1Z3
Billed to: Redwood, Inc (US)
Amount: $9,500
Tax: none shown
```

sanjay-vendor: Hi, Sanjay from Analytica Labs. We provide model evaluation services performed in India. Our accounting is worried about 30% US withholding. We asked Redwood to gross-up the invoice so our bank receives $9,500 net. Is that possible? Also, we heard about the US-India tax treaty; can that reduce withholding?

sarah: Tax team: Good questions. Short answer: we generally do not gross-up. For withholding we need either (A) a completed W-8BEN-E from the vendor certifying foreign status and any treaty claim, plus supporting documents, or (B) evidence that services are foreign-source and thus not US-source (statement about where services were performed). The US-India tax treaty can reduce withholding for certain types of income, but professional service fees are often still taxable unless specific treaty articles apply. W-8BEN-E allows vendor to claim treaty benefits, but they must supply a US TIN in some cases.

mike: Sales note: the PO explicitly asked to bill Redwood, Inc for procurement centralization reasons. @lina-sales can you ask account if billing can be changed to Redwood EMEA (UK) to avoid US withholding?

lina-sales: Will check with account manager. Quick aside: vendor said they can provide a Certificate of Tax Residency (Form 10F equivalent) from India if we need that for treaty claims.

sarah: Certificate of tax residency may help support a treaty claim but isn't a substitute for a properly completed W-8BEN-E. If vendor wants to claim treaty relief, they should: (1) complete W-8BEN-E, (2) indicate the treaty article and rate claimed, (3) provide India tax residency certificate if required by our payroll team for third-party validation. We'll validate and accept if documentation supports reduced withholding.

nora-finance: Vendor also asked how long withholding refunds take if we mistakenly withhold and they claim later.

sarah: Refunds: if we withhold and vendor later establishes treaty entitlement, reclaiming excess withholding is cumbersome. The vendor could file for refund with the IRS (Form 843/1042-S process) or we could file a refund claim on their behalf in limited cases, but both are slow and not guaranteed. That's why W-8 in advance is preferred.

sanjay-vendor: We're not familiar with W-8BEN-E. Can Redwood provide a template or help completing it? Also, we may not have a US TIN. How critical is that?

sarah: We can send a W-8 guidance doc. If vendor claims treaty benefits that require a US TIN, they may need to obtain an ITIN or provide country-specific documentation; without a US TIN, treaty benefits for certain payments might be disallowed and higher withholding could apply. However for certifying foreign status (not claiming treaty benefits) W-8BEN-E without a US TIN is usually acceptable.

mike: Lina: if account can accept being billed to Redwood UK instead, that'd likely avoid US withholding. Please check.

lina-sales: Account replied: they prefer US billing but can accept UK if vendor completes onboarding changes; it may delay PO acceptance by ~48h. Customer asks if this is the only path.

sarah: Options summary for vendor: (1) Complete W-8BEN-E (preferred) and return signed PDF + statement of where services performed. Finance will validate and likely pay gross if foreign-source is confirmed. (2) Claim treaty via W-8BEN-E and provide India tax residency certificate; we'll validate but may still need vendor US TIN depending on treaty article. (3) If vendor refuses W-8 and billing must remain US, we will withhold 30% on reportable US-source services. We do not gross-up. (4) Re-bill to non-US Redwood entity to avoid US withholding (sales to coordinate).

invoicebot: INV-AL-0326 uploaded to NetSuite. Hold code: W8_REQUIRED.

sanjay-vendor: We'll try to complete W-8BEN-E tonight. Can you DM the guidance? Also can you confirm whether a signed vendor statement saying "all services performed in India" is sufficient to avoid withholding?

sarah: A signed statement of performance location helps but isn't conclusive alone. We'll use it along with the W-8 to assess source. If all services were performed entirely outside the US and vendor certifies that, we generally treat it as foreign-source and no withholding applies. Still, W-8BEN-E is required to document foreign status.

nora-finance: Sounds good. Action items: (1) Mike/lina to check possibility of rebilling to Redwood UK, (2) Sanjay to provide signed W-8BEN-E + performance statement, (3) Finance to validate and release payment if docs sufficient.

mike: I'll chase account manager.

sanjay-vendor: Thanks  we'll send W-8 draft + signed performance statement tonight. Appreciate the guidance.

nora-finance: Closing hold once W-8 validated.
